column1: # Compiler declarations referenced only BY NAME from outside the Lean environment, so the
# dead-code finder (scripts/tests/check_dead_code_ratchet.sh) cannot see the reference: a gate
# elaborates a Lean heredoc against it, greps `def X`, or names it in a containment check. Each
# row is a ROOT of the reachability walk. Columns: the declaration (its full user name), a file
# that references it by name (the gate checks the file mentions the short name), and why.
# A row is refused when its declaration is reachable without it: the allowlist holds only what the
# environment cannot see. A gate-only API listed here is tested but unused by the compiler; when
# its gate goes, so does the row (and the declaration becomes a NEW unreachable one).
